reran: cmd.sh on w4-int, w3-base and 2.13.18: VerifyError (Inconsistent stackmap frames at branch target 48) without flags, AnalyzerException in applyOrElse with -opt:local. w4-int already contains retronym/scala#605, so that PR does not fix it. Scala 3.7.4 runs my ordinary variants correctly. On JDK 17: 2.13.8 and 2.12.16 run the finding's program and my collect variant correctly; 2.13.9 and 2.12.17 fail.
user_impact: Any non-switch match producing a value class, with a try/catch arm, where the match's value is boxed as a whole: xs.collect { case x => x match { case d: Double => Meters(d); case s: String => try Meters(s.toDouble) catch { case _: NumberFormatException => Meters(0) } } } fails with VerifyError. A type ascription in a boxed position does it without any match or partial function: def a(s: String): Any = (try Meters(s.toDouble) catch { case _: NumberFormatException => Meters(0) }): Meters. A plain lambda, a method returning the value class, an argument position (uncurry lifts there) and a switch match (boxed per case) are all fine.
fixability: clear cut: where erasure boxes a value class (new VC(e)) around an expression that may hold a try with catch, bind it first ({ val x = e; new VC(x) }), or keep adaptations of Block(_, LabelDef) inside the matchEnd label when the adaptation is a value-class box. No binary cost; a local and a store per affected site.
regression: in 2.13.9 / 2.12.17 for the partial-function and nested-match route: scala/scala#10028 (2190befafd, 'Prevent Erasure from pushing an adapt onto matchEnd labels') boxes Block(_, LabelDef) from outside. The ascription route is older (2.11.12 and 2.13.8 fail).
links: CF3 (retronym/scala#605): same family, a try uncurry leaves in place that a later phase puts behind a non-empty stack; #605 covers receivers rewritten to ScalaRunTime calls and singleton type tests, not value-class boxing, and is already on w4-int. scala/bug#12550 (closed) is the value-class receiver case (`(try new Opt(..) catch ..).orSelf`) that uncurry now lifts. scala/bug#12993 (open) is the String-concatenation case.
note: Mechanism confirmed: after uncurry, the try is the argument of matchEnd5 (stack empty, not lifted); after erasure the whole inner block becomes the argument of new V0(...) because matchEnd3's parameter is B1 (Object) and erasure boxes Block(_, LabelDef) from outside, so NEW/DUP are on the stack when the handler is entered. The partial function is not essential: it only supplies a label of erased type Object around a match typed at V0; a type ascription does the same. The constant-false guard only stops patmat making a switch. The fix belongs in erasure, in a separate pull request in the CF3 family rather than on #605: uncurry cannot predict the box because it depends on the erased type of the enclosing position, and the regression came from an erasure change. Severity raised to critical: it compiles and fails at load time in plausible code since 2.13.9.
